Potential deserves more than a college name
Little work history
A graduate resume rarely contains much workplace evidence. Give applicants a relevant exercise that lets them demonstrate reasoning, communication or a practical skill without requiring experience they have not had the opportunity to acquire.
Many colleges, one brief
Different drive schedules can distract from the vacancy itself. Establish the capabilities needed by the receiving team and use the same stated criteria for comparable positions, rather than making institution names the basis of a shortlist.
Results need explanation
A large intake does not remove the need for careful review. Ask hiring managers which responses matter, how concerns will be examined and what additional conversation a promising fresher should receive before an appointment decision.
Plan the drive around the first job
Choose the starting level
Begin with the work a new joiner will undertake. Combine library and custom questions, then configure difficulty, duration and scoring. A blended assessment can address several relevant skills without expecting every graduate to demonstrate specialist knowledge unrelated to the position.
Assessment setup
Collect useful applications
Use XoForms for branded application intake with video, written and structured responses. Ask students for information connected to the graduate role. Describe the assessment stages clearly, and use supported invitations or API workflows to coordinate the next step rather than promising unlimited drive capacity.
Application intake
Run the remote exercise
For virtual campus recruitment, configure identity checks, browser controls and AI-assisted proctoring. Students can demonstrate relevant knowledge away from a physical drive venue. Establish a way to investigate session flags and candidate explanations; safeguards do not guarantee that every concern has one interpretation.
Remote assessment safeguards
Prepare the shortlist discussion
Read actionable reports before deciding who progresses. For developer roles, examine submissions evaluated against test cases and performance criteria. Supported ATS integrations exchange invitations, scores and statuses, helping the recruiting handoff carry assessment evidence into the next human conversation.
ATS handoff
Start with assessments suited to the brief
Published tests below are starting points. Check each scope and difficulty before selecting it for a fresher cohort.
Placement aptitude
Consider this campus-placement assessment when the brief calls for aptitude evidence. Confirm its listed content against the intake requirements instead of assuming every graduate vacancy needs the same screen.
Aptitude Test For Campus Placement
Logical reasoning
Choose reasoning questions when drawing a supported conclusion belongs to the role. Explain the expected level and discuss uncertain reasoning at interview rather than equating an isolated result with overall potential.
Logical Reasoning Test
Use a communication starting point for roles involving clear explanations or team exchanges. Read the test scope first, then add fictional employer-written situations only where they address an actual job requirement.
Communication Online Test
Python foundations
For programming intakes, review the Python test and select an appropriate level. A small implementation task can provide a concrete basis for discussing the submitted code and its validation with a technical interviewer.
Python Online Test
Spreadsheet skills
Check spreadsheet knowledge where entry-level responsibilities include working with structured information. Set expectations around the tasks graduates will encounter, rather than assuming advanced spreadsheet expertise is required for every business position.
Excel Online Test
Abstract reasoning
Review this published assessment when abstract reasoning belongs in the selection brief. Keep its purpose explicit and combine the result with relevant practical evidence, candidate context and the receiving team’s judgment.
Abstract Reasoning Test
Build the evidence a graduate recruiter needs
Blended skill selection
Combine aptitude, non-technical knowledge and role-specific questions. The library supports question selection, while custom content lets your specialists introduce an appropriate engineering or business scenario without implying every prebuilt test includes that scenario.
Explore product
Code that can be discussed
Adaptive coding assessments, a live coding environment and automated evaluation provide implementation evidence. Use test-case results to prepare questions about the graduate’s choices, not to promise error-free hiring or guaranteed workplace performance.
Cognitive and behavioral context
Psychometric testing covers cognitive ability, personality and behavior through Big Five and DISC. Consider its relevance to the vacancy and interpret it alongside other evidence; it does not guarantee culture fit or lower attrition.
Structured first conversations
AI Interviews supports role-contextual questions, configurable scoring and follow-ups. Candidates complete on their own schedule, while transcripts, summaries and scores help recruiters identify areas to explore with the hiring team.
Branded application intake
XoForms supports branded video-first applications with written and structured responses. This established form capability is distinct from a promise that every test or report can be fully white-labelled for each college or employer.
A considered review
Actionable assessment reports give reviewers evidence to discuss. Agree how assessors will interpret responses and proctoring concerns before the drive, keeping the shortlist accountable to job requirements rather than an unexplained score.

Campus recruitment questions
Can we combine aptitude and technical questions in a campus assessment?
Yes. Library and custom questions can be combined, with configurable difficulty, duration and scoring. Start with the graduate role and select the dimensions that matter. Core engineering, coding or business knowledge should be assessed where relevant, not added to every intake simply because the platform supports different question types.
How should we approach fair assessment-led shortlisting for freshers?
State job-relevant criteria before comparing applicants and give reviewers a clear explanation of what the exercise is intended to establish. Consider candidate context and investigate ambiguous results. Consistent criteria can support a considered process, but the platform does not promise bias-free selection, guaranteed culture fit or a particular hiring outcome.
Does remote proctoring prevent every instance of cheating in a college drive?
No such guarantee is made here. Identity checks, browser controls and AI-assisted proctoring help flag suspicious activity. Lockdown Browser provides additional session restrictions. Decide who will review the evidence and how students can explain a concern, keeping an integrity investigation separate from the assessment of their knowledge.
Can our placement team use automated video interviews?
AI Interviews supports questions based on role context, configurable scoring and follow-up questions. Candidates complete on their own schedule, and recruiters receive transcripts, summaries and scores. Use that material to prepare further discussion rather than assume automated evaluation determines which student will succeed after joining the organisation.
What connects a virtual campus recruitment drive to our ATS?
Supported integrations move assessment invitations, scores and statuses both ways. APIs and webhooks can create assessments, invite candidates and receive results for a custom workflow. Confirm your intended connector and handoff with Xobin before the drive; this does not establish native support for every college system or learning platform.
Are these tests guaranteed to match every entry-level role?
No. Published test pages provide a starting point whose scope should be reviewed against your own intake. Configure the assessment level and add relevant custom questions where needed. A fresher finance position, software development role and engineering vacancy can require different evidence even when all applicants are recent graduates.
What should we prepare for a campus recruitment software demonstration?
Bring the first-job responsibilities, candidate stages and a proposed assessment brief. Include the college-drive schedule, remote assessment concerns and required recruitment handoffs. Ask to examine the application, exercise and reporting experience against those needs, and confirm capacity or security requirements directly instead of assuming an unlimited commercial entitlement.
